newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX index ends on record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX index ends on record closing high.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index ended the day at a record closing high on Wednesday, with sentiment during share dealings boosted by early advances on Wall Street and the ongoing strength of the dollar.

The blue-chip IBIS DAX index ended at 4,458.66 points, up 80.96 points or 1.85 percent, having hit an all-time high of 4,462.99 points late in the day. Earlier the DAX index ended up 40.03 points at 4,421.72 points, also a record closing high.
"The fundamentals right now are actually very good to keep on posting gains but the buy orders are lacking at the moment," said one Frankfurt dealer.
The market continued to focus on banks amid ongoing speculation for more mergers after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank last week announced plans to merge.
Deutsche Bank AG ended the day nearly four percent higher at 124.75 marks, a rise of 4.55 marks.
Dealers said that the share benefited from an analysts' meeting in London. "The meeting seems to be over and the orders are coming in," one dealer said.
"The entire board with Rolf Breuer at the head presented themselves very well to the investment community," he said.
BHF-Bank AG said on Wednesday it expected to post a satisfactory overall profit for 1997 after group pre-tax profit rose 10.4 percent to 181 million marks in the first six months.
Shares in BHF, considered a top takeover target, ended down 70 pfennigs at 58.30 marks even though some dealers said the results were generally in line with market expectations.
Commerzbank AG also performed strongly over the day, rising 1.07 marks at 62.06 marks.
Dresdner Bank AG fell on profit-taking over the day, but pared losses to end the day up 98 pfennigs at 84.80 marks.
Hypo-Bank ended up 1.05 marks at 77.30 marks, while Vereinsbank advanced 3.37 marks to 102.75 marks.
"The whole sector is up on speculation for more deals," said one trader. "It's a key factor driving the DAX higher."

Among other shares, carmaker Volkswagen AG ended up 33.40 marks at 1,384.45 marks after saying in recent days that it was adding extra shifts at some VW and Audi factories due to high demand for models.
